title: H-1B Visa Requirements 2026: Full Guide
metaDescription: H-1B visa requirements 2026: the 85,000 cap, wage-weighted selection, $215 registration, employer sponsorship, fees and the step-by-step process.
headline: H-1B Visa Requirements 2026

sections.title: What Is the H-1B Visa?
sections.content:
The H-1B is a US nonimmigrant work visa for foreign professionals in specialty occupations that require at least a bachelor's degree in a specific field. There is no self-application route: a US employer must sponsor you, register you, and file the petition on your behalf.

The job must qualify as a specialty occupation, meaning it requires theoretical and practical application of highly specialised knowledge, and you must hold a relevant degree or equivalent. Typical fields include engineering, IT, medicine, accounting, law, and architecture.

sections.title: The Annual Cap and Wage-Weighted Selection
sections.content:
Each fiscal year, USCIS may approve up to 85,000 new cap-subject H-1B petitions: 65,000 under the regular cap and 20,000 reserved for holders of a qualifying US master's degree or higher. Universities and non-profit research organisations are cap-exempt and can sponsor without limit.

Since February 27, 2026, selection is wage-weighted rather than random. A Level IV wage registration receives four entries in the pool, Level III gets three, Level II gets two, and Level I gets one. Higher-paid candidates therefore have a better chance of selection.

sections.title: Fees and the $100,000 Proclamation
sections.content:
Registration costs $215 per beneficiary, paid by the employer. Government fees on a typical new petition run from roughly $1,900 for a small employer to over $7,000 for a large one, before legal costs. Premium processing via Form I-907 costs $2,965 and guarantees a decision within 15 business days.

A $100,000 charge on some new petitions was created in September 2025 but was struck down by a court in June 2026 and is still not being collected, although the underlying proclamation was extended to September 2027. Two further changes are proposed but not in force: a $103,265 fee and removal of the 60-day grace period after job loss.

sections.title: The Application Process Step by Step
sections.content:
First, secure a job offer from a US employer willing to sponsor you. Each March, the employer registers you in the USCIS online account and pays the $215 fee; for fiscal year 2027 the window ran March 4 to March 19, 2026. USCIS runs the weighted selection in late March and notifies selected employers by March 31.

If selected, the employer obtains a certified Labor Condition Application from the Department of Labor, then files Form I-129 starting April 1, within a 90-day filing window. Employment starts on October 1 or later. After approval, you complete Form DS-160 and attend a visa interview at a US consulate before travelling.

faqs.q: What are the requirements for an H-1B visa?
faqs.a: You need a job offer from a US employer willing to sponsor you, a role that qualifies as a specialty occupation requiring a bachelor's degree in a specific field, and a relevant degree or equivalent. The employer must obtain a certified Labor Condition Application and file Form I-129 with USCIS. You cannot apply for an H-1B on your own.

faqs.q: How does the H-1B lottery work in 2026?
faqs.a: Since February 27, 2026, the H-1B selection is wage-weighted, not random. A Level IV wage registration gets four entries, Level III gets three, Level II gets two, and Level I gets one. The annual cap is 85,000 visas: 65,000 regular and 20,000 for US master's degree holders. Registration opens each March.

faqs.q: How much does an H-1B visa cost?
faqs.a: Registration costs $215 per beneficiary. Government fees on a typical new petition range from about $1,900 for a small employer to over $7,000 for a large one, before legal costs. Premium processing costs $2,965 for a decision within 15 business days. The $100,000 proclamation payment was blocked by a court in June 2026 and is not being collected.

faqs.q: How long does the H-1B process take?
faqs.a: The full process runs from March registration through to October employment. Registration opens in March, selection happens in late March, petitions can be filed from April 1, and work starts October 1 or later. Regular processing takes two to six months, while premium processing guarantees a decision within 15 business days for $2,965.
